question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (3)
solution:
The correct answer is '**leave**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__ ** 

__
 
• The passage talks about Sudama and Krishna not giving up hope of meeting again after losing touch. 
 
• The verb should indicate the act of not abandoning hope. 
 
• "**Leave**" fits well because it correctly completes the phrase "they did not leave the hope," indicating they retained hope. 
 
• Other options ("**leaving**", "**leaves**", "**left**") do not fit correctly in the context. 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: * The two, Sudama and Krishna, were (1) **inseparable**__. To date, their oneness is an example of true friendship ahead of the planet. This is often the rationale why they are remembered (2) __**on**__ the auspicious day of Friendship. Even after losing touch for several years after finishing their studies together, they did not (3) __**leave**__ the hope of meeting again. Sudama always had lord Krishna in his heart and soul and kept (4) _______ of him until they met again. The entire incident when Sudama met Krishna after numerous years is so (5) _______ and unforgettable. * 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** __Additional Information__ ** 

 
• Leaving: "Leaving" is the present participle form and does not fit the structure following "did not." 
 
• Leaves: "Leaves" is the third person singular form and does not fit the structure following "did not." 
 
• Left: "Left" is the past tense form and conflicts with the auxiliary "did," which demands the base form.
